findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed soda nozzle for Dr. Pepper to be soiled with organic matter. PIC was informed and nozzle was replaced. Ensure nozzles are cleaned frequently to avoid accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer buckets to have too low concentration to properly sanitize food contact surfaces. The PIC stated that the buckets are replaced daily. It’s likely the sanitizer is evaporating too much in that time. Buckets should be created more frequently to avoid dilution of sanitizer. Spray bottles with appropriate concentration were available to use instead, so the violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the 2-door glass freezer in the back room to have accumulated food debris. The cabinet holding oven racks in the front was also heavily soiled with food debris. Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to avoid accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop sink to be separated from the wall. Remove old caulking and reseal sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed personal items stored with food for the consumer in the walk-in cooler. PIC was informed and planned to get a labeled storage bin to hold personal food items to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. 
This item was marked due to the violation #16 cold food out of temperature. Rack of sandwiches and four tubs with hot dogs/sausages were left outside of the walk in cooler for an extended period of time.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.
Various sandwiches, wraps, hot dogs are observed on a speed rack with internal temperatures between 50F and 60F. The food was discarded in the dumpster. The managers stated that they removed the speed rack and cart from the walk in and when stocking beer and did not put it back into the walk in cooler.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival, no CFPM was available. PIC stated that they were moved into their position just after the last round of classes approximately eight months ago. Rebecca Armold has a CFPM that expired 2 months ago during the pandemic. Per current SCDPH policy, CFPM certifications are being honored through the end of the pandemic. Due to this, the violation is being considered corrected.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Temperature of egg salad sandwich from Deli Express case is 45°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was seperated and Deli Express personel were called to properly count and discard food.  The independant thermometer reads 41°F for air temperature at the back of the unit. This isnot sufficient to maintain food in an overly stocked unit at 41°F or below. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B). PBJamwich is set aside for Circle K to call and determine if the refrigerate statement on the sandwich is for quality or safety.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: 4-204-112  (C) A properly placed thermometer is not provided in the walk in cooler. Provide thermometer in the warmest part of the cooler to accurately monitor milk and deil itmes such as tornados and hot dogs. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: In the walk in cooler: Boxes of burgers, chicken patties, and pork ribs were observed to be at 46F also Milk is observed to be 50F. Milk was removed to go back and boxes of foods were discarded. The manager did not want a list of foods per quantity. Approximately two boxes of each chicken, pork and beef were destroyed.  750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Suggest moving the food away from the door and making sure that the defrost cycle does not move food into the temperature danger zone.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: Upon inspection, the walk in cooler door states that the internal temperature is 45F. The manager states that the unit was worked on recently. The manager is calling for maintenance to come and work on the cooler.  750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below. Keep temperature logs on the unit.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: The ice coffee machine does not contain a thermometer. Also an independent thermometer would be advised in the walk in cooler. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: Observed food service employee to have touched her hair and then not wash hands when doing food preparation. Also, hand wash is required at every glove change. Employees were coached on hand washing frequency requirements. 750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Observed boxes of cups on the floor in the dry storage area. Also, observed pizza boxes stored unprotected in the dry storage shelves. Provide protection for these single use items stored on the shelves. Take care when handling and tagging not to contaminate the food contact surfaces of these boxes. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: The metered faucet at the first hand sink in the men's restroom is turning off immediately after it is turned on. Repair to comply with the plumbing code for time of operation.  750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above). Observed cheese and chilli sauces held at 110 degrees in a dispenser. Substances where temped using an IR then probed in a cup. The thermometer on the dispenser was also reading 110 degrees. As they had been in the machine more than four hours, inspector directed the person in charge to discard the product and have the company come to assess the machine for calibration and/or repair.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Whipped topping was observed at ambient temperature (dispensed product 75F-76F). Labeling on package stated product may be held at ambient temperature for 5 days. The container of whipped topping currently in the dispenser was not labeled with the date. Manager removed and discarded the product in question. Proper date marking of whipped topping was discussed. Make sure all staff understand requirements for dating of the product once opened and to discard on the 5th day. (i.e. opened today 8/3; discard by 8/7).
  
Properly date mark the whipped topping and do not hold at ambient temperature beyond manufacturer's time frame of 5 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - Raw bacon was observed on shelving above/next to ready to eat foods in a reach-in cooler. Products were rearranged to allow for proper storage of raw bacon below all other items.

All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat and chlorine test kits were observed to have water damage. Test kits were discarded. Inspector provided some chlorine test strips to use with bleach until quat sanitizer and test strips are received later today.
Obtain and use proper chemical test kits of verifying sanitizer concentrations.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Store did not have any quat sanitizer available for use. Manager stated sanitizer was on the truck order to be received later today. In the meantime, a bleach solution was prepared at the 3 part sink (100ppm) to allow for proper ware washing (bottle of bleach obtained from grocery area).

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) F'real milk shake wand (dried milkshake splash); 
B) detachable pieces of cappuccino machine (powder buildup);   and
C) inside microwave at food counter (dried food splash)>

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) under equipment on food counter (dust/crumbs);
B) freezers holding tornados, sandwiches, and packaged ice cream (frost/general debris);  and
C) inside cappuccino machine (general surfaces - powder buildup).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
Clean inside storage cabinets at food counter as needed, especially under the hot case adjacent from the entrance (dust accumulation beginning to form).

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap and paper towels were not available at the food counter handsink. Soap and paper towels were provided during the inspection.

Maintain soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Open packages of Ballpark franks, cheddarwurst, and pepperjack sausage did not have proper date marks. Hotdogs only had delivery date on box (3/24). Other two items had delivery date (3/19 & 3/26) on the box as well as the freezer pull date (4/1). Manager and staff were advised on proper date marking once packages are opened. Benefit of doubt was given. All products were dated/kept for use.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours must be dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Once the original packaging is opened the 7 day clock begins. For example, sausages and hotdogs opened on 4/2 must be used or discarded by the end of the business day on 4/8.
Bulk creamers and whipped topping in self-serve dispensers at coffee counter must also be dated once opened and used or discarded w/in 7 days.
Properly date foods and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Items delivered last Friday were observed on the floor in the back storage area. Boxes of food in direct contact with the floor included iced tea and Gehl's chili and cheese sauces. Items are to be placed in proper storage area later today.

B) Packages of hotdogs and sausages were observed open in such a manner as the product remaining in the packaging was not covered properly. Manager was advised to maintain packaging in a manner that will allow for products to be properly covered (i.e. open at one end rather than in the middle and seal with a clip) or provide food grade storage containers.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Store foods up off the floor at least 6 inches. Keep foods properly covered between uses to protect items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Damp wiping cloths were observed out at food counter. One was sitting next to the sani-bucket behind the handsink. The other wiping cloth was observed between the creamer dispenser and cappuccino machine. 

Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. If task is interrupted, place the wiping cloths in solution. Do not leave wiping cloths out on counters for later use. If wiping cloths are no longer needed, then place them in the proper soiled linen storage area.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) soda nozzles (mold);
B) inside microwaves (food splash);   and
C) F'real smoothie mixing wand (food splash).

Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4 hours after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
Keep track of time for items such as cutting board, knives, pizza slicer, F'real mixer, tongs, and make sure these items are going through manual ware washing up to every 4 hrs. F'real mixing wand and all other surfaces around the wand need to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized just like any other food contact surface

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) Box of Polar Pop straws was observed on the floor in back storage area (received during Friday delivery). Product was to be placed in proper storage area later today.

B) Single use gloves were observed out of box in white storage tub at back food prep. Single use gloves were in contact with oven mitts and food crumbs in the bottom of the storage tub. Gloves were discarded in the trash. Keep single use gloves in original packaging until ready to be used.

C) Container of coffee filters was observed sitting out at food counter without a lid. Keep filter container covered between uses.

Single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.
